values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/blindsucker1 ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Blind Sucker #1: nightly fee $20; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boating access site on the Blind Sucker Flooding; paddlers' carry-in access about 25 yards from the parking area or directly from some campsites. The Blind Sucker Pathway runs through the campground.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/blindsucker1 ('There are vault toilets', 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well', 'A boating access site is located on the Blind Sucker Flooding', 'Carry-in access is located approximately 25 yards from the parking area, or directly from some campsites'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/blindsucker1 ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis', 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay') + amenity table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com': no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 17 sites 'suitable for tents, small trailers and large trailers'. No length limit posted. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/blindsucker1 ('Offering 17 sites suitable for tents, small trailers and large trailers', 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + amenity table (17 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic Lake Superior State Forest campground on the Blind Sucker Wildlife Flooding, 34 mi NW of Newberry via M-123 and CR-407. Fishing and paddling on the flooding; Lake Superior is a 0.8-mile hike on the Blind Sucker Pathway or a half-mile drive west on CR-407. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 17 sites for tents/small/large trailers, $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, boat access on the flooding, first-come only, 15-day max (all confirmed); season open all year, roads not plowed (already manual, matches); phone 906-658-3338 (Muskallonge Lake SP) matches.
